title: Two-Step Equations
subtitle: Equations & Inequalities: px + q = r
bounds: PROTOCOL 4a, tightened. Forms px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, and inequalities of the same shapes; one variable, never on both sides (grade 8). p has size 2-10; every solution (or inequality boundary) is a whole number of size 2-10; every division is exact and a times-table fact (p times the solution). T1 and the T4 stories have no negatives: p 2-9, q 1-12 (stories 2-12, never equal to p), r 1-20 (stories 2-20), so px is at most 19, or 32 when q is subtracted. T2 and T5 symbols carry signs as the concept: q has size 1-12 and r size at most 12 (every + and - step uses literals of size at most 12), and px has size at most 24. Groups p(x + q) = r (T3, T4): r = p times s, with p and the group value s of size 2-10 (r at most 100), q of size 1-10 (2-10 where the p is distributed), and x = s - q. Inequality stories: p 2-9, boundary 3-10, q 2-12, r at most 20.

tiers.name: Solve px + q = r
tiers.description: Undo the plus or minus first, then undo the times. Whole numbers only.

tiers.name: Negatives
tiers.description: Same two steps with negative coefficients, constants and answers.

tiers.name: Parentheses
tiers.description: Solve p(x + q) = r by dividing first, and distribute the p.

tiers.name: Stories: Write & Solve
tiers.description: Turn a short story into a two-step equation, and solve it.

tiers.name: Two-Step Inequalities
tiers.description: Solve px + q > r and friends. Flip the sign when you divide by a negative.

SAME_OP.student: Undo + with −, and − with +, on both sides.
SAME_OP.teacher: Applies the constant's own operation to the right side instead of undoing it (2x + 6 = 14 gives 14 + 6 = 20, so 10).

DIVIDE_FIRST.student: Dividing must hit every term. Safer: undo the + or − first, then divide.
DIVIDE_FIRST.teacher: Divides only the right side by the coefficient and leaves the constant alone (2x + 6 = 14 gives 14 ÷ 2 − 6 = 1).

ONE_STEP.student: You stopped early. After undoing + or −, divide to get x alone.
ONE_STEP.teacher: Stops after the first inverse step and reports the value of px (2x = 8 answers 8) instead of x. Same stop for an inequality boundary.

MULTIPLIED.student: x is multiplied by the number, so divide to undo it. Don't multiply again.
MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies by the coefficient instead of dividing (2x = 8 gives x = 16).

SUBTRACTED.student: 2x means 2 times x. Undo times by dividing, not subtracting.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Reads px as p + x and subtracts the coefficient (2x = 8 gives 6).

SIGN_DROP.student: Same signs divide to positive; different signs divide to negative.
SIGN_DROP.teacher: Loses a negative sign in the division, so the answer has the opposite sign (−2x = 6 gives 3, not −3).

WRONG_INVERSE.student: Undo the number inside the parentheses with the OPPOSITE operation.
WRONG_INVERSE.teacher: Undoes the group's constant with the wrong operation (3(x + 2) = 21 gives 7 + 2 = 9).

DROPPED_P.student: Divide by the number outside the parentheses first. Don't skip it.
DROPPED_P.teacher: Ignores the factor outside the parentheses (3(x + 2) = 21 gives 21 − 2 = 19).

PARTIAL_DIST.student: The number outside multiplies EVERYTHING inside the parentheses.
PARTIAL_DIST.teacher: Distributes to the first term only (3(x + 2) becomes 3x + 2), or writes the group as p times x plus q.

DIST_LAST_ONLY.student: The number outside multiplies the x too, not just the number.
DIST_LAST_ONLY.teacher: Multiplies only the constant inside the parentheses (3(x + 2) becomes x + 6).

DIST_SIGN.student: Keep the sign of the inner number when you multiply it.
DIST_SIGN.teacher: Loses the minus sign when distributing (3(x − 2) becomes 3x + 6), or adds one that is not there.

ADDED_FOR_MULT.student: Distributing means multiply, not add: 3 times 2 is 6.
ADDED_FOR_MULT.teacher: Adds the outside number to the inside constant instead of multiplying (3(x + 2) becomes 3x + 5).

IGNORED_FIXED.student: Don't forget the one-time amount. Take it off first, then divide.
IGNORED_FIXED.teacher: Leaves out the fixed amount: divides the whole total by the rate, or writes px = r.

ADDED_FIXED.student: The one-time amount is already inside the total. Undo it with the opposite.
ADDED_FIXED.teacher: Adds the fixed amount to the total instead of removing it (16 + 4 = 20, so 10 instead of 6).

SWAPPED.student: Numbers in the wrong spots. Match each number to its job in the story.
SWAPPED.teacher: Swaps two numbers: puts the rate on the constant and the fixed amount on the variable (4r + 2 = 16), or the total with a part.

WRONG_OP.student: Right numbers, wrong sign. Does the story add to the total or take away?
WRONG_OP.teacher: Writes the constant with the wrong operation (2r − 4 = 16 for a fee that is added).

COMBINED_TERMS.student: A number and a term with a letter are unlike. Don't add them into one.
COMBINED_TERMS.teacher: Adds the coefficient and the constant into one term (2r + 4 = 16 becomes 6r = 16).

NO_FLIP.student: Dividing by a negative FLIPS the sign: < becomes >, ≤ becomes ≥.
NO_FLIP.teacher: Divides both sides by a negative number and keeps the inequality sign.

FLIP_WRONG.student: Only flip the sign when you divide by a NEGATIVE. Here it stays.
FLIP_WRONG.teacher: Reverses the inequality after dividing by a positive number.

BOUNDARY_ONLY.student: That is only the boundary. An inequality has a whole range of answers.
BOUNDARY_ONLY.teacher: Solves it as an equation and writes x = boundary.

STRICT_VS_INCLUSIVE.student: Check the sign: ≤ and ≥ include the number, < and > do not.
STRICT_VS_INCLUSIVE.teacher: Confuses strict and inclusive: includes the boundary when the problem excludes it, or the reverse.

WRONG_DIRECTION.student: Check the words: at most and under mean less, at least and over mean more.
WRONG_DIRECTION.teacher: Reads the story's direction backwards (at most gives ≥, at least gives ≤).
